question: My client earns 95k and has a 60k deposit. How much can they borrow with this lender?
reply:
I can't work that out — borrowing capacity depends on serviceability, liabilities, dependants and the lender's own calculators, and that's a call for the broker to make with full financials, not something I can derive from a rates page.

What I can tell you from the document: the Example Lender page (read 13 Oct 2026, 12:00pm Perth time) only lists interest rates and fees by LVR band for the Basic Home Loan — it doesn't contain any borrowing power or serviceability figures at all, so there's nothing in it to calculate from even indirectly.

If it helps, here's what the page does show for the LVR bands relevant to a 60k deposit scenario (depending on purchase price, this could land in different bands):

LVR 60% or less: 6.04% p.a. (comparison 6.07% p.a.), no monthly fee
LVR 60.01% to 80%: 6.14% p.a. (comparison 6.17% p.a.), no monthly fee
LVR 80.01% to 90%: 6.44% p.a. (comparison 6.47% p.a.), monthly fee not shown (blank)
LVR 90.01% to 95%: 6.84% p.a., comparison rate not shown (blank), $10 monthly fee

If you give me the purchase price you're working towards, I can tell you which LVR band that falls into — but the actual borrowing capacity needs to go through proper serviceability assessment.
